root_cause.text: The sync_inodes_sb() function unconditionally waited for flusher threads to complete writeback on filesystems like FUSE that cannot guarantee data persistence, causing suspend-to-RAM hangs when the flusher thread blocks on operations that depend on frozen user-space daemons.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that prior to the fix, sync_inodes_sb() would call wb_wait_for_completion() (via wait_sb_inodes()) even for filesystems with no data integrity guarantees. The CVE description explicitly states: "Prior to this commit, mappings with no data integrity guarantees skipped waiting on writeback completion but still waited on the flusher threads to finish initiating the writeback. Waiting on the flusher threads is unnecessary." The stack trace shows the hang occurring at wb_wait_for_completion() → sync_inodes_sb() during pm_fs_sync_work_fn(). The fix introduces a SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY superblock flag that allows sync to skip waiting on flusher threads entirely for such filesystems, replacing the ineffective per-inode AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag that still required waiting on flusher threads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect optimization that skipped writeout completion wait for non-data-integrity mappings, ensuring all pending writebacks are properly waited for.
intent_record.what: Removed the `mapping_no_data_integrity(mapping)` condition from the if statement and deleted the associated comment explaining that mappings without data integrity semantics do not need writeout completion.
intent_record.how: This change removes a skip condition that previously allowed the loop to bypass waiting for writeout completion on mappings lacking data integrity semantics. Now the function will wait for writeout completion on all mappings that have pending writeback, regardless of their data integrity guarantees.

intent_record.intent_summary: Skip full writeback synchronization for filesystems with SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag by early return after triggering flusher threads, avoiding unnecessary blocking for non-persistent storage.
intent_record.what: Added a new conditional check after the noop_backing_dev_info return statement that tests if the superblock has the SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag set. If true, it calls wakeup_flusher_threads_bdi() with WB_REASON_SYNC and returns early, skipping the subsequent WARN_ON and writeback completion logic.
intent_record.how: This change allows filesystems marked with SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY to bypass the full synchronous writeback completion wait in sync_inodes_sb(). Instead of waiting for writeout to complete, the function now just triggers flusher threads and returns immediately. This is appropriate for filesystems that cannot guarantee data persistence anyway, avoiding unnecessary blocking.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove incorrect no_data_integrity flag setting that was incompatible with writeback_cache mode.
intent_record.what: Removed the call to `mapping_set_no_data_integrity(&inode->i_data)` from within the `if (fc->writeback_cache)` block and converted the multi-line if statement to single-line format by removing braces.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the setting of the no_data_integrity flag on the inode's address space mapping when writeback caching is enabled. At runtime, inodes with writeback_cache enabled will no longer have the no_data_integrity property set, potentially affecting data integrity guarantees during memory reclaim operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark FUSE filesystems as not providing data integrity guarantees by setting the SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag during superblock initialization.
intent_record.what: Added a single line `sb->s_iflags |= SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY;` in the fuse_sb_defaults() function to set the SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag on the superblock's iflags field.
intent_record.how: This change sets a flag that marks the FUSE filesystem superblock as not providing data integrity guarantees. At runtime, this flag will be checked by the kernel to determine whether data integrity verification (such as IMA signature verification) should be applied to files on this filesystem. By setting this flag, FUSE filesystems are explicitly marked as not supporting data integrity checks.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY superblock flag to indicate filesystems that cannot guarantee data persistence on sync.
intent_record.what: Added a new superblock flag macro SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY with value 0x00008000 to the superblock flags definitions in linux/fs/super_types.h
intent_record.how: This change introduces a new capability flag that filesystems can set to indicate they cannot guarantee data persistence on sync operations. This allows the VFS layer and applications to detect and handle filesystems with weaker data integrity guarantees appropriately.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag from mapping_flags enum to clean up the interface.
intent_record.what: Removed the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY enum constant (value 11) and its associated comment from the mapping_flags enum definition.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates a flag that was previously available to mark address space mappings as having no data integrity guarantees. Code that relied on checking or setting this flag will no longer be able to do so, and the bit position 11 is now available for potential future use.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove unused AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag accessor functions from the address_space API.
intent_record.what: Removed two static inline functions: mapping_set_no_data_integrity() which sets the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag, and mapping_no_data_integrity() which tests that flag.
intent_record.how: This change removes the ability to set and query the AS_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag on address_space structures through these helper functions. Any code that previously called these functions will no longer compile, forcing callers to either be removed or refactored to use alternative approaches.

relevance_review.reason: The group's changes remove optimizations and flag settings related to writeback_cache mode, but the root cause is about sync_inodes_sb() unconditionally waiting for flusher threads on filesystems that cannot guarantee persistence (like FUSE). The group addresses writeback completion guarantees and flag compatibility, which is orthogonal to the core issue of preventing unconditional waits on filesystems with blocking user-space dependencies. The fix should involve conditional waiting based on filesystem type, not removing optimizations in writeback_cache mode.

This group directly addresses the root cause by implementing a mechanism to skip full writeback synchronization for filesystems (like FUSE) that cannot guarantee data persistence. The early return after triggering flusher threads prevents the sync_inodes_sb() function from unconditionally waiting for completion, which was causing suspend-to-RAM hangs when flusher threads blocked on frozen user-space daemons.

This group directly addresses the root cause by marking FUSE filesystems with SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag during superblock initialization. This flag would allow sync_inodes_sb() to skip unconditional waiting for flusher threads on FUSE filesystems, preventing the suspend-to-RAM hangs caused by flusher threads blocking on operations dependent on frozen user-space daemons.

This group directly addresses the root cause by introducing a mechanism (SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag) to identify filesystems like FUSE that cannot guarantee data persistence. This flag enables sync_inodes_sb() to conditionally handle such filesystems differently, preventing unconditional waits on flusher threads that could cause suspend-to-RAM hangs.

This group removes an unused flag and its accessor functions as a cleanup operation. It does not address the core vulnerability issue, which is that sync_inodes_sb() unconditionally waits for flusher threads on filesystems like FUSE that cannot guarantee data persistence. The fix would require conditional waiting logic or special handling for such filesystems, not removal of an unused flag.

candidates.rationale: This is the check that should have been extended to also handle SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY filesystems. The vulnerable code only checks for noop_backing_dev_info but fails to skip synchronization for FUSE and other filesystems that cannot guarantee data persistence, causing the function to unconditionally wait for flusher threads that may block on frozen user-space daemons.

This early return only executes for noop_backing_dev_info. The vulnerability exists because there is no corresponding early return for filesystems with SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag, causing sync_inodes_sb() to proceed with full writeback synchronization for FUSE filesystems, leading to suspend hangs.

This line marks the point after which the function continues with full writeback synchronization. For FUSE filesystems without the SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY check, execution proceeds past this point and blocks on flusher thread completion, causing suspend hangs when user-space daemons are frozen.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional check at line 2929 only guards against noop_backing_dev_info but fails to also check for SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag. This incomplete condition allows FUSE and other non-persistent filesystems to proceed past the early return, causing sync_inodes_sb() to unconditionally wait for flusher threads that may block on frozen user-space daemons during suspend-to-RAM.

This early return at line 2930 only executes for noop_backing_dev_info filesystems. The vulnerability manifests because there is no corresponding early return for filesystems with SB_I_NO_DATA_INTEGRITY flag, causing execution to continue with full writeback synchronization for FUSE filesystems and leading to suspend hangs when flusher threads block on frozen user-space operations.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 006a0973ed020a81fe1f24b511ce9feb53f70e44
Author: Tejun Heo <tj@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Aug 25 14:11:52 2015 -0400

    writeback: sync_inodes_sb() must write out I_DIRTY_TIME inodes and always call wait_sb_inodes()
    
    e79729123f63 ("writeback: don't issue wb_writeback_work if clean")
    updated writeback path to avoid kicking writeback work items if there
    are no inodes to be written out; unfortunately, the avoidance logic
    was too aggressive and broke sync_inodes_sb().
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The root cause was that sync_inodes_sb() unconditionally waited for flusher threads, but the prior commit e79729123f63 added a bdi_has_dirty_io() check that caused sync_inodes_sb() to skip waiting when there were no dirty inodes detected. This broke the function because: (1) I_DIRTY_TIME inodes don't contribute to bdi_has_dirty_io() tests and were being skipped, and (2) inodes taken off lists during writeback could cause the function to return while writebacks were in-flight. The fix removes the problematic bdi_has_dirty_io() shortcut from sync_inodes_sb() (line 2283: changed from 'if (!bdi_has_dirty_io(bdi) || bdi == &noop_backing_dev_info)' to 'if (bdi == &noop_backing_dev_info)'), ensuring it always calls wait_sb_inodes(). It also updates bdi_split_work_to_wbs() to consider b_dirty_time lists for WB_SYNC_ALL writebacks (lines 851-854). This commit is the fix, not the bug-introducing commit.

Author: Jan Kara <jack@suse.cz>

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The root cause was that sync_inodes_sb() unconditionally waited for flusher threads on filesystems with noop_backing_dev_info (like FUSE), causing suspend hangs. The commit adds a check at lines 1403-1405: 'if (sb->s_bdi == &noop_backing_dev_info) return;' which prevents sync_inodes_sb() from queuing work and waiting on filesystems that cannot guarantee data persistence. This early return prevents the problematic wait_for_completion() call on line 1408 from being reached for noop_backing_dev_info filesystems. The same protective check is also added to writeback_inodes_sb_nr() at lines 1318-1319. This is a fix commit, not a bug-introducing commit.
